<findings>
<finding task="0"><quote>R1.3 **`compatibility`.** When present, a string of 1–500 characters after stripping.</quote><plan>R1.3: `compatibility` is "a string of 1–500 UTF-8 bytes after stripping".</plan><fix>This line sits under "Values copied verbatim from the spec" but changes the spec's unit from characters to UTF-8 bytes. Quote R1.3 as written: "a string of 1–500 characters after stripping". If bytes are preferred, raise it at plan review as a spec-level decision and add an amendment to Task 1. Delete the unlogged "R1.3's cap guards a stored field…" constraint line.</fix></finding>
<finding task="3"><quote>R1.3 **`compatibility`.** When present, a string of 1–500 characters after stripping.</quote><plan>if not (isinstance(compat, str) and 1 <= len(compat.strip().encode('utf-8')) <= COMPATIBILITY_CAP):</plan><fix>Measure `len(compat.strip())` in characters. Make the error message and the test name say "characters" rather than "bytes". Add a test that a non-ASCII value of 500 characters passes. Alternatively, keep bytes only after an owner-approved Task 1 amendment to R1.3.</fix></finding>
<finding task="0"><quote>R3.8 **Execution proof**, one time, recorded in the plan's completion notes.</quote><plan>## Decisions</plan><fix>The plan header has no `## Review Focus` section, which the template requires. Add one before Decisions, listing the five most likely uncovered failure modes, for example: a non-ASCII `compatibility` value; an invocation inside a references/ file of another skill; a pyproject-bound run of an installed llm-wiki copy; a CRLF or BOM SKILL.md under the body-length count; a `LICENSE*` copy edited in only one place. Add a pinning test for each in the task whose code would fail.</fix></finding>
<finding task="0"><quote>R1.9 The module docstring describes the new rules and the `--strict` flag</quote><plan>def _check_invocation_parity(skill_dir: Path, fm: dict) -> list[str]:</plan><fix>The plan is many times longer than the spec and transcribes full function bodies that the signatures and tests already determine. Examples: `_check_invocation_parity`, `bundled_license_violations`, `required_imports`, `check_script_headers`, `resolve_bundled_script`, `strict_violations`, `skill_body_warning`. Replace each body with its signature, the pinned values and the test assertions. Keep the exact copy (prose edits, the R3.5 sentence, the R3.6 value) and the helper scripts' non-obvious algorithms.</fix></finding>
<finding task="1"><quote>CLAUDE.md's Commands section gains the `--strict` invocation with one line on when to use it</quote><plan>- **D7** (owner, plan review, 2026-10-18): Task 7 names `--strict` in the frontmatter lint's existing CLAUDE.md comment and adds no line. Applied in: Task 7.</plan><fix>D7 changes what R1.9 requires: there is no invocation line, only an appended comment clause. That makes it a spec-level decision, so Task 1 needs an amendment block that rewrites R1.9 to match, tagged `(owner, plan 53, 2026-10-18)`. D7's "Applied in" should then read "Task 1 (spec amendment), Task 7".</fix></finding>
<finding task="0"><quote>**State test changes as +N deltas** against the suite, never absolute totals.</quote><plan>(22, 9, 27, 268, 7, 10, 29, 129 with 3 skipped, 11.)</plan><fix>Several expectations state absolute totals: this list, the Task 3–12 "Expected: `45 passed` (+4)"-style lines, "1083 passed to 1121", and "3 failed, 61 passed". State each as a delta only, for example "+4 passed, no new failures" or "suite count unchanged". Expected RED results should name the failing tests rather than total counts.</fix></finding>
</findings>
